record.context_brief: Effective higher-genus GW methods for compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds
record.original_question: Find effective mathematical methods for computing the higher-genus Gromov–Witten invariants of compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds. The paper presents this as a general problem motivated by the fact that exact formulas would follow from progress on the KKV conjecture for K3 surfaces, while existing mathematical methods are still less effective than the holomorphic anomaly equation from topological string theory in many examples.

evidence.quote: A solution to Q8 would provide a large class of exact formulas for higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.
Q9. Find effective mathematical methods for calculating the higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth compact Calabi–Yau threefold, i.e. a smooth projective complex 3-fold with trivial canonical bundle and $H^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X)=0$. For each genus $g\ge 0$ and each effective curve class $\beta \in H_2(X,\mathbb{Z})$, let $\overline{M}_{g}(X,\beta)$ denote the moduli space of stable maps from genus $g$ nodal curves to $X$ representing $\beta$, and let
$$N_{g,\beta}(X) \;=\; \int_{[\overline{M}_{g}(X,\beta)]^{\mathrm{vir}}} 1 \;\in\; \mathbb{Q}$$
denote the corresponding Gromov–Witten invariant, defined by integration against the virtual fundamental class of the (virtually zero-dimensional) moduli space.

Develop effective mathematical methods (algorithms, closed-form expressions, recursions, or structural theorems) for computing the invariants $N_{g,\beta}(X)$ for all $g\ge 2$ and all $\beta$, on compact Calabi–Yau threefolds $X$ such as the quintic threefold in $\mathbb{P}^4$. The methods should match or surpass, in computational effectiveness, the BCOV holomorphic anomaly equation from topological string theory together with its physical boundary conditions.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the problem was posed. Mathematical frameworks including the MSP/log GLSM theory of Chang–Guo–Li–Li–Liu, NMSP and a Castelnuovo-bound proof for the quintic, structural/polynomial-structure theorems, and a genus-two mirror theorem have produced effective algorithms for higher-genus GW invariants of the quintic up to relatively high genus, partially matching BCOV predictions. However, a fully effective method valid for all genera and all compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds, comparable in scope to the holomorphic anomaly equation, has not been achieved, so the problem remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Structure of Higher Genus Gromov-Witten Invariants of Quintic 3-folds
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes structural results determining higher-genus GW invariants of the quintic.
status_evidence.claim: Mathematical structural theorems now allow computation of higher genus GW invariants of the quintic threefold.

status_evidence.title: Castelnuovo bound and Gromov–Witten invariants of the quintic 3-fold
status_evidence.snippet: Talk announcing a proof of the Castelnuovo bound and explicit higher-genus computations for the quintic.
status_evidence.claim: Significant mathematical progress on higher-genus GW invariants of the quintic post-2010.

status_evidence.title: A mirror theorem for genus two Gromov-Witten invariants of quintic threefolds
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a mirror-symmetry-based formula for genus 2 GW invariants of the quintic.
status_evidence.claim: Genus 2 GW invariants of the quintic admit an effective mirror formula.
